Sam: Heads-up: forecasting shows we might hit p99 blow-ups for short-seq workloads next quarter. Need to run some admission-control math.
Priya: Can you paste the numbers? what's baseline qps, GPU pool, avg tokens, target p95/p99?
Sam: Baseline: hosted text-gen qps ~1200 overall, ~65% small-seq (<=128 tokens). Targets: p95 120ms, p99 280ms. Current us-west pool: 40 A100s reserved, avg util ~82%.
Marco: We should convert to GPU-hours + latency headroom. If we keep 20% headroom for failover, that leaves ~32 GPUs for traffic -> 32*24 = 768 GPU-hours/day.
Priya: Back-of-envelope: assume effective service μ ≈ 120 req/s per GPU for small-seq with batching & KV cache. Share numbers please.
Sam: Using 120 req/s/GPU -> 32 GPUs * 120 = 3840 req/s capacity. Our small-seq slice at 1200 qps = 780 req/s. Capacity looks OK but p99 spikes happen during bursts. From traces 95th burst multiplier ≈ 2.5.
Lina: Do the admission-control threshold calc. We need a concrete cap so queueing doesn't push p99 > 280ms. Erlang C or M/M/c sketch will help.
Marco: Quick sketch:
```
λ = arrival rate (req/s)
μ = service rate per GPU (req/s)
c = number of GPUs
ρ = λ / (c * μ)
Use Erlang-C to estimate P(wait) and expected wait time -> add to service time for p99 estimate.
```
Priya: Plugging μ=120, c=32, λ=1950 (780*2.5) -> ρ ≈ 0.508. Erlang-C P_wait ≈ 0.02 -> p99 wait ~30ms -> p99 ≈ service(≈120ms) + wait ≈ 150ms. Good.
Sam: But at peak multiplier 3.2 (observed in last Nov peak) λ≈2496 -> ρ≈0.65 -> P_wait increases and p99 crosses 280ms. So static sizing won't protect worst-case.
Marco: So options: 1) extra GPUs for seasonal headroom; 2) admission control to cap bursts; 3) degrade to cheaper model / lower-fidelity path; or 4) enterprise bypass for reserved customers.
Priya: Cost ballpark: adding 8 extra A100s to cover multiplier 3.2 costs ~8 * $1/hr * 24 ≈ $192/day -> ~$5.8k/month. (Replace $1/hr with exact vendor pricing later.)
Sam: For SRE ops I recommend two-pronged: short-term admission-control + burst autoscale; long-term reserve extra for Nov-Dec and negotiate enterprise SLOs.
InfraBot: [autoscale] policy=burst-autoscale-us-west would have triggered at 2025-11-27T15:03:12Z. Action blocked: region quota reached. See /incidents/INC-4321.
Lina: I'll open a capacity request to infra-ops for +10 GPUs for the seasonal window and add an AC rule. @Sam can you add thresholds to routing config and PR the change?
Sam: Will do. Proposed threshold: small-seq admission-control cap = 2000 req/s for us-west; enterprise bypass up to their reserved qps. I'll post a PR in ~10m. :thumbsup:
